column2: How do I search for an ancestor in old newspapers (Gallica, RetroNews, Europeana)?
column3: On their record, “📰 In the media” block → “🔍 Old press”: the full-text search opens in your browser with their name, the place and the period. Gallica (BnF) is free; RetroNews is partly paying (some newspapers and full reading require a subscription); Europeana brings together newspapers from all over Europe. To keep an article: image, PDF, screenshot or saved page, or “🔗 Paste a link” (the newspaper, the date and the page are filled in when the address gives them) → an “📰 In the media” entry with the newspaper, the date, the page, the link and the copied text. If a site changes its address: “⚙️ Site addresses”.

column2: How do I find an ancestor on a war memorial (MémorialGenWeb, 1870, civilian victims)?
column3: On their record, “Poilu 14-18” block: “🗿 War memorial (MémorialGenWeb)”; or “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”, “Wars and memorials” section. You will also find the dead of the 1870-1871 war and the civilian victims of 1939-1945 there. The search opens in your browser (the app never connects to these sites). Then “⤒ Import the record…”: the photo of the memorial or the saved page goes into the media, a source is created with the link, the death and the unit are suggested (only if they are missing), everything stays “To check” and “↶ Undo” removes everything. In a municipality monograph, “🗿 War memorial” opens its memorial. The addresses of these sites could not be checked: if one no longer works, change it in “⚙️ Site addresses”.

column2: How do I find an ancestor’s grave and keep its photo?
column3: On their record, “Cemetery” block: “🔍 Search for the grave” opens Cimetières de France, BillionGraves (with the GPS position) or Geneanet’s grave surveys in your browser, with the name and years filled in. Save the photo, then “⤒ Import a grave photo…”: it goes into the media and into the burial’s “Dated photos”; if the record does not have a burial yet, the app offers to create it (cemetery, commune, plot, GPS) and the interment if it is missing. Nothing is replaced; “↶ Undo” removes everything.

column2: How do I find a village’s population since 1793 and its old names (Cassini, EHESS)?
column3: Charts → Municipality monograph → “🏘 Population since 1793 and old names”. “↗ Open the commune on the EHESS site” (“Des villages de Cassini aux communes d’aujourd’hui”) opens your browser; save the page or copy the table, then “⤒ Import the table…”, or “✎ Copy by hand” (“1793: 512”, one year per line; “✓ Understood: …” below). A year already noted is never replaced; “↶ Undo” removes the import. The old names are matched with INSEE’s changes since 1943 (old borders supplied with the app). The monograph then shows the population curve.

column2: Where did my surname live between 1891 and 1990 (Géopatronyme)?
column3: In “Search the Internet” (record): “Géopatronyme”; or in Charts → Surname map: choose a name, then “🔤 This name on Géopatronyme (1891-1990) ↗”. The map of births by department opens in your browser; the app does not connect to it.

column2: How do I search the registers of Europe (Matricula, Norway, Sweden, Denmark, Ireland, Bohemia, Hungary, JewishGen) and among Huguenots or seafarers?
column3: On the record, “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”, “Europe · Registers and archives” section (Matricula is searched by place: the parish) or “Protestants and seafarers” (Huguenot refugees, merchant navy crew lists). Everything is free; JewishGen requires creating a free account. Then “⤒ Import what you found”: the image of the record or the saved page goes into the media, a source is created with the link and the page, and the record is suggested (baptism, burial, census, emigration…; never a second baptism or death). Pasted links from Matricula, Digitalarkivet, Riksarkivet or irishgenealogy.ie are recognised (register, page).

column2: How do I import an article from a foreign newspaper (Chronicling America, Trove, Papers Past, Delpher)?
column3: On their record, “📰 In the media” block: “🌍 Foreign press” opens the search in your browser (name and years filled in). Then “⤒ Import (foreign)…”: as for Gallica, the article becomes an “In the media” entry with its source and its link; the date and the page are read from the link when it gives them (Chronicling America, Papers Past). “↶ Undo” removes everything.

column2: How do I find a prisoner of the Great War (Red Cross, ICRC)?
column3: On their record, “Military” or “Poilu 14-18” block: “🌍 Prisoners 14-18, Arolsen…” (or “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”). The ICRC site (grandeguerre.icrc.org) does not keep the name in its address: “📋 Copy the name and open” puts “SURNAME First name” on the clipboard and opens its search page; paste it into the box. Then copy the text of their entry or save the image, then “⤒ Import…”: the ICRC entry goes into the media, a source is created with the link, the “Prisoner of war” event (date and place of capture, camp) and their unit in the Poilu block are suggested. Nothing is replaced; “↶ Undo” removes everything. The app never connects to the site.

column2: How do I find out whether an ancestor was a deputy, a senator, an inventor, a doctor or a Polytechnique graduate?
column3: “Search the Internet” → “🔍 Online archives…”, or the buttons in the “🔬 Science, inventions”, “🎓 Diplomas and education” and “🧩 This person was…” blocks: Sycomore (former deputies), former senators, invention patents 1791-1902 (INPI), medical theses (Sudoc, BIU Santé), registers of the École polytechnique, directory of learned societies (CTHS). When importing a copied entry: a patent becomes a 💡 invention with its patent (the “Inventor” profile is ticked), a thesis or Polytechnique a 🎓 diploma, a term of office a 🏛 mandate (political profile). Everything stays “To check” and can be undone with “↶ Undo”.

column2: Where do I search in Paris, in museums and in local history books?
column3: Village record: “🌍 Books and archives on this place…” opens Internet Archive and Persée on the name of the place (local history books and journals), and, for Paris, the reconstructed civil registers (before 1860) and the electoral lists (1860-1932) of the Archives de Paris. The Joconde database (museums of France) searches for an artist by name. For a book or article found, “⤒ Import…” stores it as a source with its link.

column2: How do I search for an ancestor in Italy, Spain, Portugal, the Netherlands, Flanders or Poland?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…” (record, “Departures / emigration” block or village record): Antenati (search by name, in addition to the search sweeps’ link), PARES (Spain), Torre do Tombo (Portugal), Open Archives (Netherlands, Flanders), Geneteka (Poland). Open Archives publishes its data: “⤓ the results as JSON” opens in your browser; save the file then “⤒ Import…”: each line (baptism, death…) becomes an event if you tick it; a marriage stays written in the source, for you to place in the family yourself.

column2: How do I search in England (FreeBMD, FreeCEN), Canada or the United States?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…”: FreeBMD (births, marriages, deaths since 1837) and FreeCEN (censuses 1841-1911) are searched with a form: the name is copied, paste it into the box. Then copy the FreeBMD results page and “🔗 Paste a link”: each line read (quarter, district, volume, page) can be ticked to become an event. In Canada: BAnQ and Library and Archives Canada; in the United States: NARA and Find a Grave (the text copied from a grave suggests the burial, the cemetery and the memorial number).

column2: How do I search the archives of Nazi persecution (Arolsen) and among the Righteous Among the Nations?
column3: “🔍 Online archives…”, “Memory of the Shoah and of persecution” section: Arolsen Archives (documents from the camps and displacements) and Yad Vashem (Righteous Among the Nations). An imported Arolsen document stays sober on the record, and that record is never used in a game (like those of deportees). A Righteous Among the Nations becomes an award in “🏆 Competitions and awards”.

column2: Where are the addresses of the online archive sites? (an address no longer works, hide a site, add my own)
column3: A single screen for all the sites: in the “🔍 Search the online archives” window, at the bottom left, “⚙️ Site addresses”. The sites are arranged by country then by theme, in sections that fold up; the 🔍 box finds a site. Write the new address with {nom}, {prénom}, {lieu}, {de}, {à}, {département}… in place of what is being searched; the switch shows or hides the site; “📒 My genealogy society” gives the address of your society for each department; “⭐ My sites” adds your own (it is also in “Search the Internet”). Everything is kept straight away (“↶ Undo”, “↺ Reset to default”), and the settings made before in each window are carried over. “Free only” (ticked at first) hides the paying sites. The badge says whether the app’s address has been checked, partly checked or not yet.

column2: How do I search FamilySearch and WikiTree from a record?
column3: “Search the Internet” block of the record → “🔍 Online archives…”: FamilySearch’s indexed records (surname, first name, place and years of birth filled in), its catalogue (which registers of a commune have been filmed) and WikiTree. FamilySearch requires a free account to see the results and the images. If the record has a FamilySearch identifier, its entry in the tree opens directly. The app never queries these sites: only the address is opened in your browser. Then “⤒ Import what you found” (or “🔗 Paste a link”): the source with the link, the missing events, and the FamilySearch identifier if there was none. A whole FamilySearch or WikiTree tree is imported as GEDCOM (Home → Import).

column2: How do I find an ancestor who left for Quebec or Acadia?
column3: “Departures / emigration” block of the record → “🌍 Quebec, Castle Garden…”: the Fichier Origine (the French who settled in Quebec from 1600 to 1865: baptism in France, parents, marriage in Canada) and the Centre d’études acadiennes in Moncton. Copy the entry found and use “⤒ Import…”: the baptism is added if it is missing, and a departure for New France goes into “Departures / emigration”, with the entry number. Nothing is replaced, everything stays “To check”, “↶ Undo” removes everything.

column2: How do I find an ancestor who arrived in New York (Castle Garden)?
column3: “Departures / emigration” block → “🌍 Quebec, Castle Garden…” → Castle Garden (arrivals from 1820 to 1892, before Ellis Island). Copy the passenger’s line (ship, port of departure, arrival date, age, occupation) and “⤒ Import…”: a journey is added to the “Departures / emigration” block, and a birth “about …” based on their age if the record has none.

column2: Did my ancestor receive the Saint Helena Medal?
column3: The soldiers of the Revolution and the Empire (1792-1815) still alive in 1857 received it: about 400,000 names. “Military” or “🏆 Competitions and awards” block → “🌍 Saint Helena medallists…” (offered if the person was born before 1810). “⤒ Import…” adds the medal to “🏆 Competitions and awards”, their birth if it is missing and their 1857 address.
